items.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: Max Steiner from the early days of film was one of the greats.

ctx.x: Who are your favorite film scorer people?

Oh gosh, well Max Steiner from the early days of film was one of the greats. I think Bernard Herrmann, who did Psycho, the movie Psycho. And he really changed the way, especially strings are scored in films. And Bernard Herrmann, he did a lot of the “Twilight Zones” early on. And then he did many of the Hitchcock films. I think he died in 1974 I believe. I think Taxi Driver was his last film. But he also did the original Cape Fear back in the 40s and the score was so great to that that when they redid it with…
